info.title: Ghar API
info.description: The API behind the Ghar web and phone apps. Generated from packages/contracts by `pnpm openapi`; do not edit by hand. Every request is scoped to the signed-in person’s household, which the server works out from the session.

get.description:
Owners and adults. The accounts the bill form offers: hidden ones are left out. By bank link,
oldest first, then by name.
By name, ignoring case. With `q`, only assets matching every word.
The asset with its jobs (soonest due first), its documents and every time a job was done.

delete.description: Deletes the asset with its jobs and their history. Its documents stay, unlinked.

get.description: What needs someone today, for the dashboard.
Who the credential belongs to and what it's scoped to. Works before onboarding.

post.description:
Emails a sign-in link that also carries a code to type into the phone. Anyone may sign up: an
address without an account gets one. The answer is the same either way.
Bearer only. Ends this device's sign-in: the access token and every refresh token descended from it.

Trades a verified code, link or refresh token for a new token pair. 401 when the code is wrong or
expired, or the refresh token has expired, been revoked or already been used.

get.description: Oldest first, the order they were connected in.

post.description: Finishes a new connection with the public token Link handed back.
A token for opening Link. With `itemId`, update mode for repairing that connection.

Turns a connection off: the access token is revoked at Plaid and nothing syncs after. Every
account, charge, category, note and trip tag it brought in stays exactly where it is. Deleting
those is a separate thing somebody has to ask for.

delete.description:
Deletes what a connection that was turned off brought in: its accounts, their charges and their
balance history. This cannot be undone, and the connection itself stays as a record that the
bank was once linked.

post.description: Finishes an update-mode Link: the connection goes back to good and catches up.
Syncs one connection now, instead of waiting for the daily run.

get.description:
Owners and adults. By name, ignoring case, each with its current due date and status. The bills
page puts late bills first; that order moves as payments arrive, so pages can't follow it.
The bill with its due dates over the last year and the next one, newest first.

post.description:
Marks a due date paid for a payment no transaction shows (cash, a card that isn't linked).
Marking one already marked keeps the first mark. Answers with the bill as getBill does.

delete.description: Takes a mark back. A transaction that pays the due date still counts.

post.description: Owners, adults and members.

put.description: Replaces every field of a native event. Synced events answer 403.

delete.description: Deletes a native event, every occurrence of it. Synced events answer 403.

put.description: The signed-in person's answer to an event they're on.

get.description: Every item from every requested source for a range of days in the household's zone.

Every calendar linked in the household. Linking happens in a browser: open
`/api/calendar/google/connect` signed in, and Google sends the person back to `/calendar`.

post.description:
Starts linking the signed-in person's Google Calendar from the phone, where the browser shares no
cookies with the app. The URL's state is signed and names who asked, and only that person can
finish. Owners, adults and members.

Finishes linking a Google Calendar with the handoff the app received. Only the person who started,
in the same household, can use it: anyone else gets 403. An expired, changed or already used
handoff gets 400; start linking again. Owners, adults and members.

delete.description: Unlinks a calendar and removes what it synced. Your own, or anyone's if you're an owner.

post.description: Syncs the household's linked calendars now, skipping any that need reconnecting.

get.description:
Owners and adults. Archived categories are included, so a bill or charge filed under one still
shows its name; offer only the others for new choices. In the household's order, then by name.

patch.description:
Owners and adults. Renames or restyles a category, or moves it among its siblings. What it is
for and where it sits in the tree stay as they are: nothing already filed under it changes.
Leave out whatever you aren't changing.

put.description:
Owners and adults. Archives a category or brings it back. Categories are never deleted: an
archived one keeps everything filed under it and every budget line it has had, and only drops
out of the pickers, the rules and what Ghar files by itself. Archiving a parent archives its
children with it; restoring brings back only the one named, and a child needs its parent back
first.

get.description:
By name, ignoring case. With `q`, only contacts matching every word, still by name so pages
hold still (the contacts page also puts names starting with the first word first).

delete.description: Jobs that named this contact keep going without a vendor.

post.description:
Emails the signed-in person today's digest now, with their chosen sections, whether or not it's
on and whether or not today's already went out. `sent` is false when there's nothing to say.

get.description: Newest first. Sensitive documents are left out for members and viewers.

post.description: Answers 422 when nothing was uploaded to the path, or it isn't a photo or PDF.

The first of three steps to add a document: get somewhere to put the file, PUT the file there,
then createDocument with the path. The bucket is private; this URL only accepts an upload.

Deletes an uploaded file that never became a document, when someone scans it and then cancels.
A file a document or renewal already uses stays.

Sends a file from createDocumentUpload to Claude to read its dates, before the document is
saved. Owners, adults and members. Photos in HEIC format can't be read; send a JPEG.

delete.description: Deletes the document and its file.

get.description: A signed link to the file that stops working after a few minutes. Ask again rather than storing it.

post.description: The same, for a document's saved file.

get.description:
Soonest first, so what has expired leads, then what's coming up. Sensitive documents are left
out for members and viewers.
Not found when it's gone, has no date it runs out, or is a sensitive document the caller can't see.

put.description: Says it won't be renewed, for this date. Saying it again changes nothing.

delete.description: Takes "not renewing" back, so reminders for its date go out again. Fine when it wasn't set.

post.description:
Moves the date on to the new term. Reminders start over for the new date, and "not renewing"
no longer applies. 422 when the date isn't later, when storagePath or issuedOn is for anything but
a document, or when nothing was uploaded to storagePath.

get.description:
Owners and adults. One month's plan against what it has spent. A month nobody has planned
answers with no lines and the spending it has anyway, so the screen can offer to plan it.

post.description:
Owners and adults. Closes a month that has ended: each line keeps the actual it finished with,
so a bank correction months later can't rewrite it, and rollover lines hand what's left to the
month after. A month that isn't over yet refuses.

Owners and adults. Brings the month before's lines across: its plans, its rollover settings,
and, once that month is closed, what each rollover line carried. Lines this month already has
are left alone.

get.description: Owners and adults. The last six months, this one included, each against what it planned.

put.description:
Owners and adults. Plans one category, or changes what it is planned. The month is created on
the first line, and a closed month refuses. A category may hold one line per month.

delete.description: Owners and adults. Takes a category out of the month's plan. Its spending stays where it is.

get.description:
Owners and adults. Oldest first, with what each one's linked account has in it today and how
that has built up.

put.description: Owners and adults. Every field is given, so leaving one out clears it.

delete.description: Owners and adults. The linked account and its balance are untouched.

get.description:
Owners and adults. The month so far in one answer: spent against the same stretch of last
month, where it went, the budget if there is one, what's on hand, and the newest charges.

Owners and adults. Every rule, in the order they run: exact merchant matches first, then by
priority, then newest. A charge takes the category of the first rule that recognizes it.

delete.description: Owners and adults. Charges the rule already filed keep their category.

get.description: Owners and adults. Spending and money in, month by month, over the last six or twelve months.

post.description: Onboarding. Creates a household and makes the caller its owner. 409 if they already have one.

get.description:
The caller's household and their role in it. 404 when they have not created or joined
one yet, which is the signal to show onboarding.
Invitations still waiting for an answer, newest first.

post.description:
Owners and adults. Emails a single-use link that expires in seven days. Inviting an address
that already has a pending invitation replaces it, so the old link stops working.

get.description: Everyone in the household, in the order they joined.

patch.description: Owners only. Nobody changes their own role, and a household keeps at least one owner.

delete.description: Owners only. Nobody removes themselves, and a household keeps at least one owner.

get.description:
What onboarding offers for a household's time zone and currency. Needs a signed-in person but
not a household, since it's asked for before there is one.

post.description: Joins the household. The caller must be signed in with the invited address.
What the accept screen shows. 404 for an unknown token.

Reads the OpenGraph tags on a page and nothing else. Not a scraper: it does not follow
the page's own links, read its body text, or run its scripts.
Checks your Gmail for new confirmations now, instead of waiting for the morning.

get.description: Your drafts waiting for review, newest email first.

post.description: Saves the booking as you confirmed or corrected it.

get.description: The signed-in person's linked Gmail, or null.

delete.description: Unlinks your Gmail and revokes Ghar's access. Drafts already made stay to review.

post.description:
Starts linking the signed-in person's Gmail, read-only, from the phone, where the browser shares no
cookies with the app. The URL's state is signed and names who asked, and only that person can
finish. Owners, adults and members.

Finishes linking Gmail, read-only, with the handoff the app received. Only the person who started,
in the same household, can use it: anyone else gets 403. An expired, changed or already used
handoff gets 400; start linking again. Reads no mail yet. Owners, adults and members.

get.description: Every job, soonest due first, then by title; jobs with no due date last.

post.description:
Mark done: logs the work and rolls the next due date one cadence past it. Logging an older
completion fills in history without moving the schedule.

delete.description: Takes back a completion logged by mistake, and works the schedule out again from what's left.

get.description: By name, ignoring case. Archived accounts only when asked for.

delete.description: Takes its values and its snapshots with it, so past net worth days lose it too. Archive to keep them.

get.description: Newest first.

post.description: Adds a value. Earlier values stay as history.

delete.description: For a value entered by mistake. Snapshots already taken keep what they recorded.

get.description: Highest APR first, the order to pay down in. Debts with no APR last, larger balances first.
Typed-in days only, newest first.

post.description: Sets the figure for a day, replacing one typed in for the same day.

get.description: What a link does and whether it can still be used. Always 200, for a link that doesn't work too.

post.description:
Does what the link says and uses it up, in one transaction. 409 when it was already used, or the
date it names has changed. 400 when it's invalid, expired or no longer allowed, or the category
isn't one of the household's (the link keeps working then). 404 when the thing it names was deleted.

get.description: By name, each with its items.

post.description:
Saving a trip's list for next time. Packed state and who was carrying what are dropped:
a template is the shape of a list, not a snapshot of one trip's progress through it.

get.description: Everyone: members first as they joined, then everyone added. A household is small, so it's one page.

post.description: Owners and adults. Someone without an account; members join by invitation.

patch.description: Owners and adults, and only for someone without an account.

delete.description: Owners and adults, and only for someone without an account. Their documents stay, belonging to nobody.

post.description:
A charge typed in by hand: the cash dinner no card will ever tell you about, or a card that
isn't connected. It belongs to no account, which is how the rest of finances tells it from a
synced one.

`amountCents` is negative for money out, as the column is. `tripId` tags it on the way in.

get.description:
Owners and adults. What the charges a list is filtered to add up to, and the same filter month
by month over the last year. Takes the list's filters.

patch.description:
What a person owns on a charge: the category it is filed under, the trip it is tagged to,
whether it counts towards spending, and a note. A null `tripId` takes it back off a trip; a
`categoryId` files it, as the digest's one-tap link does, and must be one of the household's
unarchived categories. Leave out whatever you aren't changing.

A category set here is a person's decision: it replaces whatever categorization decided, and
nothing automatic changes it again.

get.description:
Owners and adults. The rule worth offering after someone files a charge by hand, or null when
there is nothing to offer: nobody filed it, it has no merchant to match on, or a rule already
sends that merchant to that category. Ask after a successful file, and offer it once.
Every booking, soonest trip first, with where its price stands.

post.description: Owners, adults and members. The price watch starts on by default.

put.description: Replaces every field. Owners, adults and members.

delete.description: Removes the booking with its price history and alerts.

get.description: Oldest first.

post.description:
Turning an idea into a trip. The idea is removed: it has served its purpose, and leaving
it on the board would have the household voting on something already decided.
Sending the vote already cast takes it back, so one tap is both vote and un-vote.

get.description: Soonest start first, then by name; trips with no dates yet last.

post.description:
Filing a booking under a trip. `addToItinerary` is on by default because the reason to
link a booking is almost always to get it onto the itinerary, where it lands as a slot
already booked. Turning it off leaves the booking attached to the trip and nothing more.

delete.description:
Taking a booking off a trip. Its option goes too, and its slot if nothing else was in it;
a slot with other options stays, reopened.

get.description:
Every open slot, most urgent first: anything with a reservation or decide-by deadline, soonest
first, then whatever happens soonest. The trip, the household's members and the whole itinerary
come too, so a decision can be made in place with what is around it in view.

post.description:
Fills the itinerary in from the trip's linked bookings, each as a slot already booked. Idempotent:
a booking that is already on the itinerary is left alone.

delete.description: Deleting is for mistakes. To rule an option out, reject it.

post.description: Settles the slot on this option. Choosing another later swaps the choice.
Rules an option out without deleting it. Rejecting the choice reopens the slot.

Lays breakfast, lunch and dinner, and a morning, afternoon and evening, onto one day. Anything
the day already has under the same name is left alone, so asking twice adds nothing.
The whole itinerary comes back, so a client never has to guess at the new order.
Brings an idea off the board with its link and picture. The idea stays on the board.

The quickest way in: paste a link. The page's OpenGraph tags fill in the title and image, read
the same way the idea board reads them. A page that will not say what it is still becomes an
option, titled with its address.
Undoes a choice or a skip. Every option goes back to being a candidate, rejected ones aside.
Not doing this one. The slot stays, quiet, so the decision is on record.

get.description: In the list's own order, then by label.

post.description:
Applying a template to a trip. Items the list already holds are skipped rather than
duplicated, so applying the same template twice is safe.

Unauthorized.description: No valid session or access token (unauthorized).

Forbidden.description: The household role does not allow this, or a cross-site cookie request (forbidden).

NotFound.description: Not found in this household, or no household yet (not_found).

InternalError.description: Something went wrong on the server (internal_error).

RequestId.description: Identifies the request in the server log. Error bodies repeat it as error.requestId.

bearerAuth.description: Ghar API access token from POST /api/v1/auth/token.

cookieAuth.name: sb-<project-ref>-auth-token
cookieAuth.description: The Supabase session cookie the web app sets when someone signs in (split into .0, .1, … when long). Writes authenticated this way must come from the site’s own origin.
